title: Understanding Data Movement in AMD Multi-GPU Systems with Infinity Fabric
problem: There is a gap between hardware capacity and achievable application performance in GPU systems. Understanding data movement characteristics and communication bottlenecks across AMD multi-GPU systems connected via Infinity Fabric is unclear.
motivation: Optimizing data movement is critical for achieving high application performance in scientific and machine learning workloads on modern multi-GPU systems.
method: The authors propose a test and evaluation methodology to characterize data movement performance on AMD MI250X multi-GPU systems. They evaluate different communication options including point-to-point and collective communication patterns, and various memory allocation strategies between GPUs and host CPU. Performance is measured on single-node setups with four GPUs, comparing latency and bandwidth across communication approaches including RCCL library and MPI-based solutions.
key_novelty: A systematic characterization methodology showing that direct peer-to-peer memory access and RCCL-based collective communication outperform traditional MPI approaches on AMD Infinity Fabric interconnects.
contributions: Test and evaluation methodology for characterizing data movement on AMD multi-GPU systems
Performance characterization of point-to-point and collective communication on AMD MI250X GPUs
Empirical validation that direct peer-to-peer access and RCCL outperform MPI in latency and bandwidth
Practical guidance for optimizing memory and communication strategies on AMD systems
limitations: Evaluation limited to single-node setups with four GPUs; multi-node scalability and larger GPU configurations not addressed.
primary_theme: Characterizing data movement optimization in AMD multi-GPU systems
